text: Canyon View Park Pond (Utah County): Because Canyon View Park Pond will be drained this summer (for dredging and deepening), we're increasing the daily limit as follows:
This change went into effect July 2, 2026 and will remain in effect until Oct. 1, 2026. We want to give anglers the opportunity to harvest more fish before the pond is drained.

notices.title: Minersville Reservoir (Beaver County)
notices.name: Minersville Reservoir
text: Minersville Reservoir (Beaver County): Because of ongoing drought-related water losses, we're changing the daily limit and regulations at Minersville Reservoir as follows:
Minersville Reservoir is open to underwater spearfishing for all game fish.

This change went into effect July 2, 2026 and will remain in effect until Oct. 1, 2026. We want anglers to harvest more of the fish in the reservoir. (Reducing the population here has proven successful at increasing the survival of the remaining fish.) Important: The reservoir's artificial fly and lure regulation will remain in effect throughout this entire period — the use of bait is not allowed.

notices.title: Pineview Reservoir (Weber County)
notices.name: Pineview Reservoir
text: Pineview Reservoir (Weber County): Because Pineview Reservoir will be intentionally drawn down this summer (to prepare for installation of a new drinking water pipeline), we're increasing the daily limits as follows:
12 largemouth or smallmouth bass (a combined total)

This change went into effect July 2, 2026 and will remain in effect until Dec. 31, 2026. We want anglers to harvest more of the fish in the reservoir. (Reducing the population will also help increase the survival of the remaining fish.)

notices.title: Crouse Reservoir (Uintah County)
notices.name: Crouse Reservoir
text: Crouse Reservoir (Uintah County): Because of low water levels and poor snowpack, we're increasing the daily limit at Crouse Reservoir to 8 trout, any species. This change went into effect on May 11, 2026 and will remain in effect until Dec. 31, 2026. The Utah Division of Wildlife Resources wants to provide anglers the opportunity to harvest more fish in hopes that reducing the population may:
Improve survival of the remaining fish.
Encourage fishing in this underutilized fishery.

notices.title: Nine Mile Reservoir (Sanpete County)
notices.name: Nine Mile Reservoir
text: Nine Mile Reservoir (Sanpete County): Because of drought-related water losses, we're increasing the daily limit at Nine Mile Reservoir to 16 trout. This change went into effect on May 11, 2026 and will remain in effect until Oct. 1, 2026. The Utah Division of Wildlife Resources is concerned that fish will not survive the summer, so we are proactively increasing the limit to:
Reduce trout densities and improve survival of any remaining fish.
Encourage anglers to make use of fish that would otherwise perish.
